reviews.text: Chris Pratt stars as a modern-day soldier drafted in to fight a war against future aliens - with clunky, predictable consequences.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text:
It’s not perfect, it won’t be the next big classic, but with greatly done action, awesome alien design, & A FANTASTIC STANDOUT PERFORMANCE from Yvonne Strahovski! 
PUT HER IN MORE THINGS PLEASE
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is one of the biggest surprises of the year, boasting an impressively creative creature design, entertaining action sequences, and a contender for the most beautiful shot of 2021.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: It’s only fitting that Chris Pratt honors his place among the Schwarzeneggers by doing the kind of sci-fi action movie Arnold would’ve done in the 90s.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: If you are looking for a thrilling terror machine, The Tomorrow War will satisfy that craving. Otherwise, it’s a lesson in overstaying one’s welcome.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: While the story builds itself around a cool and interesting concept, it’s the sheer action spectacle that stays with you.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: As far as the performances go, Pratt serves his role better than it serves him, and Simmons is terrific as usual.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: ...sporadically watchable yet predominantly mediocre...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: "The Tomorrow War" is a serviceable action film that could certainly scratch the itch many have right now for a giant summer blockbuster, but the weak script keeps the movie firmly in mediocre territory.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: From the characterisation to the horrendous dialogue, everything is lacking. Even the complex action scenes are spoiled by hysterical editing.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Everything onscreen becomes either a product of embarrassingly bad screenwriting or an homage to a better landmark in the genre, often both.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The film, directed by the man behind The Lego Batman Movie, delivers a fun time and the entertainment you probably need after a long day. At the same time, it appears to be more of a one-time watch and nothing more than just a decent summer sci-fi flick.
reviews.author: Zofia Wijaszka

reviews.text: Every scene is taking from another piece of the modern science fiction lexicon. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martinez

reviews.text: Slick to a fault, and clumsy in the extreme, this big-budget alien war flick hasn't a lick of wit or cleverness.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is a fun, mindless, alien invasion popcorn flick that would've benefited from a theatrical release in more normal times. It's truly the epitome of what a summer blockbuster is and should be.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: With a more solid script that paid just a little more attention to things like sense and logic, the film could have easily been so much better.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Amiable popcorn fare, then, but a little more creative effort might have made this really special.
reviews.author: Trevor Johnston

reviews.text: A two-headed popcorn filler that is part sentimental family fodder, part save humanity from the evil ancient aliens, it won't be winning any awards but it's big and brash enough to keep you entertained.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: It suffers from inane dialogue and a superficial story driven by explosions and aliens that reminded me of the dinosaurs from Jurassic Park.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: Chris Pratt is likable enough in this unique action-packed film, but it wasn't serious enough to be a super-thriller, or funny enough to be an action-comedy.
reviews.author: Vincent Schilling

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is not only a canny audience grab, it's also a devastatingly perfect encapsulation of masculinity today.
reviews.author: Tracy Clark-Flory

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is like the Golden Retriever of movies
reviews.author: Robert Slack

reviews.text: If you parse its time-travel paradoxes for even a minute or two, the whole movie falls apart. But if you're the kind of person who likes this kind of thing, here it is.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: It's that signature concoction of brain and brawn that helps Pratt produce another crowd-pleasing and humanistic action hero, something that seems to come to him naturally.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It's a floor-shaking blockbuster of the purest kind, with terrific set pieces and tonnes of fun.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Cool creature design, an intriguing premise that doesn't reach its full potential due to its horrible dialogue, and Pratt's lack of dramatical acting skills. An average-level sci-fi action movie, sadly.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Narratively padded and visually overstuffed with CGI, The Tomorrow War plays out like Starship Troopers drained of Paul Verhoeven's subversive satire.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: As a film about time travel that offers thrills while actually making coherent sense, this alien invasion onto Amazon Prime is welcome.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: Make the mistake of thinking too deeply about the story and you'll discover - surprise, surprise - that the proceedings don't really make much sense...[it's] straight-up cheeseburger cinema, another example of a B-movie with A-grade production values.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War plays out like an alien action movie mixtape as it shamelessly steals from every film in its genre, from Aliens to Starship Troopers.
reviews.author: Ray Gill Jr.

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War has got a trashy popcorn vibe to it that it wholeheartedly embraces, and a cornball machismo that you can't help but get taken in by.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: The jovial/likable Chris Pratt persona is a miscast in this aliens invasion movie.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Watchable and diverting but still pretty standard issue sci-fi (therefore likely to be forgettable) with Daddy Issues Drama X 2. In its particulars pretty damn silly.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Everything that I liked was in concept and on paper, but when you watch it, it just kind of comes across as a generic sci-fi action movie.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: An unimaginative sci-fi action epic that squanders a promising premise, thanks to subpar action, and a star that it has no idea what to do with
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Cool critters foiled by every time-travel trope ever... as if someone transplanted a great idea for a monster movie into the cheapest derivative script available...
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Chris Pratt was always an unlikely hero... in his new sci-fi action vehicle "The Tomorrow War," his heroism is more unlikely than ever.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: It's too damn long, but at least this time travel romp has good comic timing.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: The filmmakers have liberally cribbed from a number of sources, resulting in a movie that feels both piecemeal and formulaic. You've seen it all before - and what you saw before was probably better.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: From a distance, The Tomorrow War seems like and OK Chris Pratt Action extravaganza. But taking a closer look plot holes and scripted nonsense start taking over, so better watch this one without paying attention to key details for maximum enjoyment.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: It does, in its cheap-and-cheerful way, have fun.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Skip the mental gymnastics and watch something else. Or buy a yo-yo.
reviews.author: Hunter Lanier

reviews.text: An adrenaline-fuelled sci-fi saga that checks all the boxes of a fun and visual effects-driven summer blockbuster. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: As good as the pitch might have been, the execution is terrible.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Convoluted and frustrating.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: It mashes up too many movies in a clumsy way, and it ruins a promising premise.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: A post-pandemic blockbuster easily digestible for comfort viewing.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War has its good and bad moments, but it mostly gets the job done, even if there's a nagging feeling that it's not quite as good as it could have been.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: At heart, this is a standard shoot-'em-up whose bad guys are such mindless flesh-eating monsters (think of the original Alien, times a zillion) that slaughtering them in ever more elaborate action sequences becomes the movie's main objective.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: Its setup is more tedious than interesting and nearly all of its dialogue is exposition; even emotional moments are just characters explaining something that happened.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: "The Tomorrow War" is the surprise of the season, a stuffed-to-the-gills battle between evil aliens and terrified humans.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Not much of it makes you give a damn, and it even wastes the talents of J.K. Simmons...
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: An over-stretched but enjoyably cheesy action epic.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War sinks under its oppressively flavorless design.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War desperately wants to be Independence Day for the 21st century, but it so fundamentally misunderstands the assignment that it's missed the science fair altogether.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The big budget stunts and explosions were money well spent.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: In the end, The Tomorrow War turns the end of the world into a damp squib.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: That odd obsessive harping on its own inconsistencies convinces me that at some point in the process this script was way better than what actually made it onto the screen.
reviews.author: Alexander Joenks

reviews.text: Maybe getting older has turned me sentimental, but I am a sucker for a movie that strives to impart something meaningful, even if it's far from perfect.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: I felt some pretty strong B-movie vibes, and when the film embraces this, it rocks extremely hard. It's when it takes itself too seriously that it ends up coming across as silly.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War hits most of its action and science fiction beats at the right frequency to recommend an evening watching it with the sound turned way up.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: A decent popcorn Summer sci-fi adventure with genuine suspense that's not afraid to be earnest and heartfelt. Best enjoyed when you don't overthink the questionable 'science' + time travel plot.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: This is the kind of junk food cinema that goes down smoothly.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Takes itself very seriously, much more than the ridiculous story allows. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: A somewhat messy story, but... well executed by McKay. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: It gives you action, drama, suspense, and some wonderful characters to fall in love with. Despite its flaws, you'll walk away being entertained.
reviews.author: Allison Nichols

reviews.text: The writing just isn't where it needs to be to justify so much of what happens in The Tomorrow War.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Exciting, escapist fun - like a futuristic 'It's A Wonderful Life' amid marauding aliens.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: An absolutely perfect summer popcorn movie... those who do make the effort to watch it on the biggest screen available to them won't be disappointed.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: This overlong Tomorrow has no tomorrow on screen.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The future is carnage, and the fights with alien monsters in an abandoned city are predictably stupid and messy.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: This is good popcorn entertainment at its finest, and if on a Friday night you're looking for something dumb, loud, and fun with incredible set pieces and monster mayhem, I say you can't go wrong with this one.
reviews.author: Grant Jonsson

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is flabby, turgid, and muddled. There are moments that rock and elements that intrigue, but the former lose their impact through repetition while the latter get lost in a lot of... well, just a lot of stuff.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Loved Chris Pratt and Yvonne Strahovski. Loved that the black people didn't die in the first 10 minutes. Loved the action.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: A big, energetic sci-fi action flick that eschews metaphysical contemplation about time travel in favor of a whole lot of blowing up buggy aliens.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War has big "lazy Sunday movie on TNT" energy and that is not a compliment.
reviews.author: Drew Dietsch

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War﻿ boasts an interesting setup and solid performances by the cast, but it still comes across as unremarkable, if standard, genre fare.
reviews.author: Chris Agar

reviews.text: Pratt, as Dan, is still a very likable character and we were drawn-in wanting to see where he and this was going. But at well over 2 hours, we wish we could have saved time traveling through this film a little quicker.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War isn't a disaster, but it could have been a lot more.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: Short-term characters manage to add dimension. Chris Pratt plays Chris Pratt, but we've gotten used to him not getting super angry about anything and still killing things with accuracy.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: ...big screen entertainment on the small screen, expensive, effective and unmemorable in its generic conventions...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Come for the big action/sci-fi spectacle, but stay for Yvonne Strahovski, Sam Richardson, and J.K. Simmons.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Millions had to die so one family could hug it out. Cool.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Zero points for originality.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: The trappings are familiar, but "The Tomorrow War" is a fun popcorn movie thanks to great special effects, a likable lead and sharp pacing.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is a movie that needed a surround sound, enormous screen experience - because its only value is in the spectacle.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Despite its flaws, The Tomorrow War is a fantastic blockbuster, a definite must-see for the summer. I only wish I had gotten to see it on a much bigger screen.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Sprawling and earnest, tense and exciting, and sometimes just plain daft, with several different films seemingly squeezed into its 138 minute run time The Tomorrow War tries to be all things to all people.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: ["The Tomorrow War"] may have been [Chris] McKay's first venture into the live-action territory but he sure has an eye for propulsive action moments and visual flair.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Had it opened in theaters as planned, a $20 ticket might feel like a ripoff. At home, it's a star-fueled spectacle that's moderately better than most direct-to-streaming films that try to do the same thing.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War will undoubtedly remind its viewers of various science fiction movies they've seen before. Still, it does boast impressive visuals and action and a surprisingly pro-science message.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: Dumb films that are secretly smart are awesome; this is a smart film that's secretly dumb, and no matter how solid the action that's not much fun at all
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War has its moments, scenes that work perfectly well as sci-fi action summer movie fare, but the intriguing premise runs out of fuel far too quickly, leaving the rest of the film in search of a point it never quite finds.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: You could probably have a field day counting how many problems The Tomorrow War has, but that still doesn't take away how much fun and exciting the experience is.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: Struggling to raise the emotional stakes beyond the level of a video game, the film's reliance on shootouts and explosions suggests, in this case, that tomorrow feels more like yesterday.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: But if I had a time machine, I'd punt myself to the past just before The Tomorrow War went into production, and save everyone the trouble.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: There are some fun scenes in it, but it's infuriating to watch if you have any sort of background in science fiction.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: I took one look at The Tomorrow War's dopey premise and knew I was all in.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: It has fun, stupid action and extremely fun, stupid science.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: [The movie] somehow make us uncertain about how everything's going to work out. It takes real skill to pull that off these days, but The Tomorrow War does it. You'll see.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: ...there is no saving the movie that tries to be the 'Every Topping' Pizza of sci-fi in 139 minutes...
reviews.author: Aniruddho Chakraborty

reviews.text: The concept of soldiers being sent hurtling through time to fight an alien invasion in the future sounds cool, but it immediately raises basic questions about logic and strategy.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: What's depressing is that the director Chris McKay is a skilled satirist who, in previous outings... gleefully pilloried the very same tired and overdone genre conventions that he presents here as straight-faced storytelling.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: This old-fashioned popcorn summer thriller with alien invaders and time-traveling heroes more than fills the bill for wild escapist fun.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: The major point seems to be action piled on more action, all revolving around a premise that tramples credibility at nearly every turn...
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: ...The Tomorrow War is just the type of escapist entertainment we need...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: [The movie] fumes of mediocrity--the underwhelming CGI, the formulaic, cliched dialogue, as well as the foreseen resolution.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: The many moving parts and oscillating tones, which could feel flimsy and cheap in less able hands, wobble and shake here and there, but ultimately hook, line and sinks, not just into the diabolical swarm of alien booty, but in the heart of the viewers.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War's high concept plot is easily picked apart by common sense and logic. What does work is an emotional core that marries well with the big-budget special effects.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: It's not that sci-fi action movies need to seem realistic. But The Tomorrow War's view of human nature feels so jarringly out of touch, it's easy to get stuck in disbelief and hard to take anything else that happens all that seriously.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: There are some entertaining moments and the movie might have played better on the big screen, but it's impossible to shake the feeling that you've seen it all before.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: They're all perfectly cast, and the movie does exactly what it sets out to do. It's all about manly men, coolly composed women, and nervous comic sidekicks joining together to load up, crack wise, and splatter the scenery with the green guts.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: As these man-vs.-human-munching-alien-creature movies go, this one from director Chris McKay and writer Zach Dean is fairly entertaining, if a little repetitive and unimaginative.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Decent enough as a diversion but something that could have been so much more.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is a great big Frankenstein's monster of a movie. It's cobbled together from pieces of other science-fiction films.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War feels absolutely massive in its scope. Every element from the story and effects, to the cast and action sequences, have the impact of a major theatrical release ... a summer film event of epic proportions.
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War pretends it's taking the high ground right as it plummets off the cliff of reason.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Like Dwayne Johnson, the Jurassic World and Guardians of the Galaxy star just has the ability to drag you along on even the most uninspiring adventure and ensure you at least have a semblance of a good time.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: It's the kind of sci-fi blockbuster where a sober military scientist (Yvonne Strahovski) yells, "Someone get a harpoon on that tentacle!" and the audience gasps, united in the hope that the weapon skewers its salivating target.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: If nothing else, it tries... What it doesn't try hard enough to be is its own thing.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Watching Chris Pratt fight to save the future has a certain appeal, but in the here and now, he can't even save the movie.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Chris Pratt's dad saves the world in derivative sci-fi effort that is 2 hours and 20 minutes long.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Well over two hours of fighting, accompanied by excruciatingly overwrought music.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: The film itself is a tired, derivative, pro-military-and-guns wannabe sci-fi film that will remind audiences of better, older sci-fi action adventure films also on streaming.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: An intermittently fun sci-fi actioner that tries to be too many disparate movies at once, and fails at executing each and every one of them. But, a tepidly fun time nonetheless.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: An action-packed summer blockbuster that comes with some of the most horrific aliens made for the big screen. Simmons and Pratt are solid, and when Yvonne Strahovski is in the movie, she delivers some big Emily Blunt energy.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Don't scrutinise this one too closely, simply let its combination of lauding smarts and practising stupidity wash over you and you'll have a fine time.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: It has been said that time travel movies are easy to do badly and difficult to do well. If that's the case, then The Tomorrow War falls into the former category.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Is it really July 4th weekend if we aren't watching a blockbuster film about the world's militaries preventing an alien invasion?
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: [It] throws "Alien," "The Terminator" and "A Quiet Place" in a blender. And, like that gross kale smoothie you made once, the result is gray goop.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: The resulting collision of tones is a bit odd, but at least that keeps things relatively unpredictable, and helps the film become something (slightly) more than its generic first impression.
reviews.author: Dominic Corry

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is a true two star movie, constantly swinging back and forth between exciting sci-fi action, and a clunky big budget bomb.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: A blandly derivative and overlong sci-fi thriller.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: The humorless "The Tomorrow War" is gobbledygook that attempts to update the "Independence Day" formula with a time-travel gimmick.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is, at heart, a movie about time and what we do with it. Fathers must learn to spend it well.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: With all the elements of a fun Summer alien invasion/time loop action film, it's unfortunate that Chris Pratt can't manage to coax the audience into caring about his fate, let alone the world's.
reviews.author: Bill Watters

reviews.text: By the time it's over, it feels like tomorrow.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: If you aren't an Amazon Prime subscriber and can't watch The Tomorrow War, don't worry that you're missing much; you've likely seen something very similar--and better--before.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: This is a massive misfire that I unfortunately never connected with on an emotional level.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War isn't as good as it could have been, but it's an entertaining enough sci-fi action blockbuster.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is the kind of movie that would play much better on a big screen, but the film still has more pluses than minuses, making it a positive experience no matter where you view it.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: 'The Tomorrow War' is another CGI action gloop-fest that's slugged its way onto Amazon Prime and has nothing to say for itself. Sure, it's going for big thrills and it's got Chris Pratt, but there's something so bland and annoyingly trite about it all.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: There's nothing 'tomorrow' about a recycled sci-fi jumble that places all its bets on yesterday.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: There are some fun moments of over-the-top alien action but generic characters and the predictability of the story blunts much of the film's excitement.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Chris Pratt is no Tom Cruise. Without the wise-cracking and cheeky grins, he seems at a loss as to what to do with his face.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: It doesn't work much as an escapist film either. Every time there's a set piece that you are mildly enjoying, something happens that spoils your immersion, be it a nonsensical sacrifice by a character, or a line of dialogue that appears out of place.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is no Edge of Tomorrow, but it's a lot like its star -- goofy, good-natured, and desperate to be liked, despite its problems. Don't burst its bubble.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Once The Tomorrow War gets clear of its clunky, half-baked set up and gets the action going, it boasts its share of viscerally enjoyable sequences.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Will fit the sweet spot for sci-fi fans looking for the next Oblivion, Edge of Tomorrow or Looper.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Wildly inventive, infectious fun
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War sticks to the essential details while allowing its charismatic ensemble and extravagant action to stand out at the forefront
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: At 140 minutes, the film may take up a lot of your time, but it's not worth any of it.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: It exists, basically, as something mostly predictable and wholly generic.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War doesn't feel like one big epic, rather three movies mashed into one. So many promising ideas crammed into a single film that never gives any of them the room to breathe.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: An ostensibly 'original' (i.e., not based on a graphic novel) but highly derivative alien-invasion meets time-travel tale.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A good movie exists within the mega futuristic world building of "The Tomorrow War," but Chris Pratt is incapable of delivering the multifaceted character scaffolding required for the action flick's deeper emotional beats.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: It's a clever premise and one that opens up many time travel paradoxes which are addressed with wit and intelligence.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The Amazon movie is your average action film with some great intense moments, but what makes the Chris Pratt movie worth watching is the ultra scary alien monsters. The creature design is the most original and scariest alien in a long time.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: The final product, at 140 minutes, warps back and forth between being a throwback with fancier effects and a fresh breeze with thrown-back irritants.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: A deeply satisfying 1990's-style blockbuster throwback, one that relishes the ability to craft its own story, designate its own rules and tell a single rollicking big-budget sci-fi action yarn over a single 138-minute feature.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: After sitting through two-plus hours, the final act is utter nonsense and a complete letdown.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: This is what summer movies are all about -- endearing but flawed humans fighting aliens as they save all of humanity and resolve their family estrangements.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The befuddled look on Chris Pratt's face in the opening shot of The Tomorrow War is an accurate reflection of how viewers may feel.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War delivers on its promise of being an entertaining and action-packed summer blockbuster.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: The surprise of the year. Not only is this an enjoyable cheesy sci-fi romp, but Chris Pratt is at his best in years.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War benefits from having such extremely high stakes, while also showing the personal cost for those enlisted in this suicide mission.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War thinks of itself as a sci-fi Saving Private Ryan or the heir to the Independence Day throne ... but has far more in common with the likes of Battlefield Earth.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is the second noisy "temporal war" movie of the pandemic era, after Christopher Nolan's Tenet. To differentiate between the two, this is the one Nolan would have written if he'd suffered a head injury.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: [A] gloriously moronic picture
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: A surprisingly terrific piece of popcorn entertainment that will blast off your home screens into a fun space.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Despite straying into predictable and contrived territory, The Tomorrow War is an engaging and entertaining sci-fi romp featuring a hugely talented cast.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: To its credit, the monster onslaughts are engaging, if for no other reason than the loud noises, continual devastation, and video game aesthetics of mowing down enemies.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Quite the adrenaline shot! An awesome Sci-Fi war action film that delivers on alien mayhem, big stakes and family drama. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Don't read too far between the lines and enjoy this giddy popcorn flick in all its chaotic foolishness. Life is short.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War provided all the alien action I wanted, but it also provided a large amount of emotion I wasn't expecting. I went in excited for the film, and it exceeded all my expectations.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: The film has lots of effects and action and loads of Chris Pratt. What it needs more of is heart.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The best thing in the movie is Pratt.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: The movie clearly intends its monsters as a metaphor for climate crisis. It works fairly well...
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: In the end, no single thing kills this movie, but an entire collection of weaknesses, from Chris Pratt's over-earnestness to the ridiculous premise to the charmless dialogue and unimaginative video game vibe.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Director Chris McKay loses all of the idiosyncratic creativity he showcased in The Lego Batman Movie to meet the needs of this lumbering star vehicle for Chris Pratt, who has skillfully transitioned into a bland silhouette of an action star.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War is little more than a clunky, Nolan-esque exercise in instruction-manual cinema.
reviews.author: Wes Greene

reviews.text: The movie accumulates much from its betters before it starts to rot from the inside. Eventually, it becomes a distended corpse of a big-ticket blockbuster, washed up on streaming.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Clichés rain as fast and as furiously as bullets.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: A somewhat fun and schlocky ride that feels like it was ripped out of the '90s, but even back then it would have felt derivative of more original sci-fi fare.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: At nearly 140 minutes in length, the production wears out its welcome, but introductory confusion is enjoyable, with the film presenting a fun ride of elaborate survival sequences.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: "The Tomorrow War" spends most of its time in the future, but its central theme is timeless: the replayed tragedy that sometimes you don't come home the same from war.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: A big, dumb, blockbuster starring Chris Pratt as a ripped science teacher who punches giant lice to death.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: It all feels like a heavy meal, and the action scenes and the creature effects are very derivative.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Despite its wild premise - Chris Pratt goes to the future to fight aliens! - and considerable talent, The Tomorrow War is mostly just bloated blockbuster business as usual.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: Unfortunately, The Tomorrow War isn't allowed to be the dumb, "just go with it" summer spectacle it should have been, a la Independence Day.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: There's also an unfocused quality to the movie's focus on humanity's prevailing can-do, science-and-family-first spirit, which makes the White Spikes, and the attendant horrors of some kind of war, seem like so much setup for an equally meager payoff.
reviews.author: Simon Abrams

reviews.text: To that end, "The Tomorrow War" was lost from the moment that mega-blockbusters got so big they could only afford to have avatars instead of protagonists.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: This is one of the most confounding and ridiculous movies of the year, with a terrific cast sinking under the weight of a convoluted plot and medium-grade CGI special effects.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Animation director Chris McKay brings the science back to sci-fi while delivering a shoot 'em up monster movie that seems tailor-made for action fans.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: While it is certainly too long, The Tomorrow War really is a fun, action packed, Sci-Fi monster movie. There is even a touching and heartwarming side to it as well.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Action-packed and family-centric in a solidly commercial way, the pic may be missing that certain something that would have made it huge in theaters, but it will be plenty entertaining as an addition to Amazon's streaming menu.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: It's a lot of deluxe pablum you've seen before, but all you can eat of it.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War should entertain you, plain and simple. It's fun and original sci-fi, done well.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War might not fully deliver on its brilliant premise, but it's still an epic and original sci-fi trip that's worth taking.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: At its core, this is just a really good monster movie. All the same, there's a touch of beauty to it.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Give McKay credit for the willingness to play to the film's strengths, using its emotional elements to enhance a film that could have easily been overwhelmed by action.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Despite the occasional arresting image ... there is literally not a single interesting idea or exciting bit of action.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Many will have a closer encounter with their screen to watch it than what could have been, but this alien invasion flick is a solid summer watch.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: The script by Zach Dean clearly draws inspiration from The Terminator combined with Independence Day. I can hear that being the pitch of the movie to the studio.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Blockbuster movies are often as loud and action-based as "The Tomorrow War," but they're rarely as diverse in tone or so delightfully wild when it comes to in-your-face entertainment.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: The Tomorrow War shatters expectations, and despite hitting a few familiar notes along the way, this surprisingly emotional action-packed blockbuster proves to be a fun ride and one that showcases the talents of Chris Pratt and Yvonne Strahovski.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: J.K. Simmons (Spider-Man) has some great dialogue as Dan's estranged father, and he delivers his lines expertly.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: A fleet-footed, good-humored, big-hearted, science-minded, sufficiently goopy, proudly goofy blockbuster boasting more temporal twists and richer text than you expect. The only regret is that its bountiful, buoyant scope deserves a bigger screen.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

synopsis: In The Tomorrow War, the world is stunned when a group of time travelers arrive from the year 2051 to deliver an urgent message: Thirty years in the future mankind is losing a global war against a deadly alien species. The only hope for survival is for soldiers and civilians from the present to be transported to the future and join the fight. Among those recruited is high school teacher and family man Dan Forester (Chris Pratt). Determined to save the world for his young daughter, Dan teams up with a brilliant scientist (Yvonne Strahovski) and his estranged father (J.K. Simmons) in a desperate quest to rewrite the fate of the planet.
